title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Late Charges and Returned-Payment Fees
content:
**Credit and collections rule — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.**

**The rule.** A late charge is the past-due room-and-board balance times the monthly late charge rate, rounded to the cent; a room-and-board month becomes past due once the late charge grace days have run from its due date. No late charge is assessed on fees or on earlier late charges, and none is assessed when the past-due room-and-board balance is below the late charge minimum. A late charge is assessed only while the agreement is active, in the notice period or discharged. Nothing is assessed while the stay is converted to another payer source, and nothing for any month the converted payer source covers. At most the monthly maximum of late charges is assessed per agreement per calendar month. A returned-payment fee is charged once per dishonored payment at the operator's fee schedule amount.

**The past-due room-and-board balance** is the total of the open balances of the agreement's room-and-board charges for every service month whose due date is more than the grace days before the assessment date; fees and late charges are left out.

**Tests read from the system record before a late charge is posted.**

| Test | Passes when |
|---|---|
| Agreement status | Active, notice period or discharged |
| Monthly maximum | The agreement has no more than the monthly maximum of late charges for that calendar month once this one is counted |
| Minimum | The past-due room-and-board balance is at least the late charge minimum |

**Hypothetical figures.** Past-due room and board of 2,600.00 at a monthly rate of 1.5 percent: 39.00. If the only open items are a returned-payment fee and an earlier late charge, the past-due room-and-board balance is nothing and no late charge arises.
